page: Amazon Web Services c7a.xlarge is a compute-optimized virtual machine instance powered by the AWS Nitro hypervisor. It features an x86_64 architecture with 4 dedicated physical cores and 4 vCPUs, utilizing the AMD EPYC 9R14 processor running at a clock speed of 3.7 GHz. The hardware configuration includes 8.0 GB of DDR5 system memory operating at 5 GHz, yielding a resource density of 2.0 GB of RAM per core. This instance does not include local storage or dedicated GPU hardware, and it provides a baseline network bandwidth of 2 Gbps.

Benchmark data indicates strong single-core performance, with the stress-ng single-core CPU test and Geekbench single-core score placing in the top 25% of evaluated servers. Single-threaded bzip3 decompression and Geekbench text processing also demonstrate strong performance. Conversely, multi-core operations, including stress-ng multi-core CPU and Geekbench multi-core tests, fall within the average range. Memory performance exhibits a notable tradeoff: cached small-block read-only memory bandwidth is average at 591.1 GB/sec, whereas uncached large-block read-only memory bandwidth and the Passmark memory score fall into the bottom 25%.

Given its compute-focused 1:2 vCPU-to-RAM ratio and dedicated CPU allocation, the c7a.xlarge is designed for CPU-bound workloads that do not require massive memory footprints. It is well-suited for single-threaded processing tasks, web serving, software compilation, and lightweight database operations. The inclusion of DDR5 memory and dedicated AMD EPYC cores provides high compute density, though the lack of local storage requires external network-attached storage for data persistence.
